result.markdown: --- title: "[vals.fmt_date()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-function}" body-classes: doc-api-page page-navigation: false html-table-processing: none --- ::: {.doc-subject} Format values as dates. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/posit-dev/great-tables/blob/main/great_tables/_formats_vals.py#L1381-L1465){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-Kind.FUNCTION} ```python vals.fmt_date(x, date_style="iso", pattern="{x}", locale=None) ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} Format input values to time values using one of 17 preset date styles. Input can be in the form of `date` type or as a ISO-8601 string (in the form of `YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS` or `YYYY-MM-DD`). ::: ## Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [x]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [X]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : A list of values to be formatted. [date_style]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [DateStyle]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [["iso"]{.st}]{.doc-parameter-default} : The date style to use. By default this is the short name `"iso"` which corresponds to ISO 8601 date formatting. There are 41 date styles in total and their short names can be viewed using `info_date_style()`. [pattern]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [str]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [["{x}"]{.st}]{.doc-parameter-default} : A formatting pattern that allows for decoration of the formatted value. The formatted value is represented by the `{x}` (which can be used multiple times, if needed) and all other characters will be interpreted as string literals. [locale]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [str | None]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : An optional locale identifier that can be used for formatting values according the locale's rules. Examples include `"en"` for English (United States) and `"fr"` for French (France). ::: ## Formatting With The `date_style` Argument {.doc-formatting-with-the-datestyle-argument} We need to supply a preset date style to the `date_style` argument. The date styles are numerous and can handle localization to any supported locale. The following table provides a listing of all date styles and their output values (corresponding to an input date of `2000-02-29`). | | Date Style | Output | |----|-----------------------|-------------------------| | 1 | `"iso"` | `"2000-02-29"` | | 2 | `"wday_month_day_year"`| `"Tuesday, February 29, 2000"` | | 3 | `"wd_m_day_year"` | `"Tue, Feb 29, 2000"` | | 4 | `"wday_day_month_year"`| `"Tuesday 29 February 2000"` | | 5 | `"month_day_year"` | `"February 29, 2000"` | | 6 | `"m_day_year"` | `"Feb 29, 2000"` | | 7 | `"day_m_year"` | `"29 Feb 2000"` | | 8 | `"day_month_year"` | `"29 February 2000"` | | 9 | `"day_month"` | `"29 February"` | | 10 | `"day_m"` | `"29 Feb"` | | 11 | `"year"` | `"2000"` | | 12 | `"month"` | `"February"` | | 13 | `"day"` | `"29"` | | 14 | `"year.mn.day"` | `"2000/02/29"` | | 15 | `"y.mn.day"` | `"00/02/29"` | | 16 | `"year_week"` | `"2000-W09"` | | 17 | `"year_quarter"` | `"2000-Q1"` | We can use the `info_date_style()` function within the console to view a similar table of date styles with example output. ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [list[str]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : A list of formatted values is returned. ::: ## Examples {.doc-examples} ::: {#a6e05364 .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} from great_tables import vals vals.fmt_date(["2025-01-01", "2025-01-02"], date_style="month_day_year") ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` ['January 1, 2025', 'January 2, 2025'] ``` ::: :::
